text:
ana: Canary rollout stalled — automated traffic shift ran but canary still at 0% in our dashboards. Argo shows the VirtualService was updated 6m ago.
deploy-bot: [automation] attempted traffic-shift for svc payments v2 -> weight 10% at 2026-03-18T14:20:34Z. status: started
mike: any errors in the gitops/app logs? maybe argo failed to sync the real manifest?

jordan: argo shows sync=Healthy, last-sync 6m ago. The VS resource in cluster is present and contains weight 10 for canary. Weird.

samir: grabbing envoy stats from the payment pods — polling envoy admin: `curl localhost:15000/stats | grep upstream_cx_active` — canary upstream shows 0 active connections.

ana: hmm could be service selector mismatch or network policy blocking sidecar traffic to canary pods.

samir: ran `kubectl get endpoints -n payments` — stable endpoints present, canary endpoints not registered (no ready pods). But the pods are Running and have LIVENESS/READINESS green in k8s.

mike: are these GPU-backed instances? any node-level taints/affinity preventing sidecar injection or readiness probes?

ana: this cluster had a TF change earlier today that added a NetworkPolicy to restrict pod egress to infra subnets (security req). copying snippet:
```
resource "kubernetes_network_policy" "restrict_egress" {
  metadata { name = "restrict-egress" namespace = "payments" }
  spec {
    pod_selector = {}
    egress {
      to { ip_block { cidr = "10.0.0.0/16" } }
      ports { port = 443 protocol = "TCP" }
    }
  }
}
```

ana: that NP looks broad (pod_selector empty) — likely blocks envoy sidecar outbound to control-plane or to kube-dns, preventing endpoints registration with sidecar. this is terraform-managed so it was applied in infra CI earlier.

jordan: that explains why Argo sees the resource but Envoy can't route — the sidecar can't reach SDS/ADS or xDS stream? Could be blocking control-plane (istiod) comms or CNI plugin control plane.

mike: also saw a spike in spot GPU preemptions around the same time — some canary pods were recreated on different nodes, maybe transient, then the NP prevented reconnect.

samir: immediate mitigation: we can patch the NP to allow egress to kube-system and to 127.0.0.1/host for sidecar, or add pod selector limiting NP to only certain workloads.

ana: can we avoid editing TF state directly? I can create an emergency k8s patch to open egress for namespace `payments` to `kube-system` CIDR and to cluster-DNS IPs. Then reconcile TF change later.

jordan: agreed — do quick patch + force traffic-shift rollback if needed.

ana: running patch now: `kubectl patch networkpolicy restrict-egress -n payments --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/egress/-","value":{"to":[{"namespaceSelector":{"matchLabels":{"kubernetes.io/metadata.name":"kube-system"}}}],"ports":[{"port":443,"protocol":"TCP"}]}}]'`

deploy-bot: [automation] emergency patch applied by ana at 2026-03-18T14:24:12Z — patch succeeded

samir: rechecked endpoints — canary endpoints now present. envoy stats show upstream_cx_active > 0 for canary. nice.

mike: can we re-run the traffic-shift automation? we should also avoid a loop where TF re-applies the restrictive NP and removes the patch.

jordan: re-triggering traffic-shift: `curl -XPOST https://traffic-api.internal/v1/shifts -d '{"service":"payments","canary_weight":10}'` — returned 202 Accepted.
deploy-bot: [automation] traffic-shift completed at 2026-03-18T14:27:50Z — canary traffic ~10% reported by ingress metrics.

ana: follow-ups: 1) open a TF change to narrow the NP podSelector to only `kind:cronjob` workloads (or add label allowlist for sidecar) 2) add an integration test in infra CI that deploys a small sidecar-equipped pod in namespaces with NetworkPolicy to validate xDS/connectivity before merge 3) add a guard in progressive-delivery workflow to check envoy upstream endpoints before committing traffic shifts.

mike: +1 on the guard, that's the real automation gap. also let's add a cost note: spot GPU churn can make canary pod rollout noisy; for critical canaries set a minimum on dedicated capacity or longer warmup.

samir: opened PR infra#428 to narrow NP and added test. tagging @security for review.

ana: thanks all. resolved for now — will follow up in infra PR. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: incident-note: canary traffic outage 6m, mitigation applied, follow-ups filed (infra#428, platform#201).
